## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22861e63ff08f3e8cec2a387bff0be185848439e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (ungoverned; `reviewFace` returns no `hits`) + scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs (judged as the contract files, per the brief)

First review of PR #34054 on this head, card #33770. Read: the card body and its three comments (triage 6893167834, the claim 6898065682, the os-dev-report 6898438400), records 6891926185, 6892305129 and 6892689104 of PR #33736, the PR body, the two-file list, the net diff against main (+90 -24), the head blobs of both files around the reader and the guard's `recordPassVerdict`, the head's `BRIEF_GRADE_LINES` and `--template` text, and the check-runs. Everything below was traced by reading; nothing was run.

Below, the two upper grade words are spelled only on the lines that name a finding, so that this record reads as it means under the reader it reviews.

Check-runs on the head, snapshot 2026-11-15T17:37Z: 53 runs; 26 success, 23 skipped, 0 failed, 4 STILL RUNNING: `Live half-state sweep`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`. Concluded success include `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size` and the PR-body guards.

### ① Derived judgments

- The closed-or-none CLEAN set only NARROWS. `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED_STATE` loses its second alternative (the full stop closing a bold title, then a sentence) and keeps the first unchanged; `contractReviewFindingContinues` can only turn a state into undefined, never the reverse. Nothing that read open at base reads closed now. Right.
- The FAIL-spelling set moves BOTH ways, as the card asks. Wider (toward refusal): `was`, a colon after `is` or `was`, a dash spaced on its left, an arrow or a struck word before the value, marks before a cell's word, a keyed cell, a header row's verdict column, any case in a heading tail. Narrower (toward clean), all through the idiom or the bare word: the value `fails closed`, `failed closed`, `fail-closed`; a bare caps FAILED line; a caps `FAIL closed` in a heading tail that is not the tail's first verdict word. Each narrowing is one the card names, except the two small ones in N3 below.
- `tableVerdictColumn` and `inTable` are the only state. Both reset on every line that does not open with a pipe, a blank line included, so nothing leaks from one table into the next or into prose; the column is taken from the first row of each run of rows only. Traced on the three-line pin: the header sets column 2, the delimiter row reads nothing, the body row reads its cell. Right.
- One reader still: no new export, `contractReviewFindingContinues` is module-private, `record-recognisers.mjs` is byte-identical to main and re-exports the same name. `recordPassVerdict` and every non-test line of the guard are untouched: both guard hunks sit inside `selfTest()`.
- `CONTRACT_REVIEW_FAIL_IDIOM` carries a `g` flag but is used only in `replace`, which keeps no position; two reads of one body still agree.
- Real records, traced by reading at base and head: 6898215827 (refused on both sides, for its count line spelled with the number after the grade word, a rule this PR does not touch), 6897840089, 6897742597, 6892689104 (clear on both), 6892305129 and 6891926185 (refused on both, open findings). The eight other CLEAR records of the PR body's list were fetched and read for a grade-led line with a closed or none state: there is none in any of them, no table row, no heading tail, no keyed line. The N1/N2 narrowing therefore moves no measured record, and the 9 clear / 9 refused claim holds as far as it was read (fourteen of the eighteen).
- The docblock agrees with the code except for one clause, raised as S2.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` label present, `Clause-②: no` on the body and the claim, `Metadata-protocol: none`; `scripts/pm/**` only, nothing published. `Check Changeset` concluded success. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation 1, the surface breach into `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`: accepted. It is self-test only (one control loses the line and is renamed, one refusal assertion is added), it is forced (the dropped line is the guard's pin on the allowance N1 removes, and would read red), and no verdict logic moves. Whether the open card the dev names on that file collides is the seat's serial check, not judged here.
- Deviation 2, the forced edit of the `#33604 r3` row (fifth cell now open): accepted. The row's title and a comment above it say why, and the cell is the exact line the card's N1 removes the allowance for.
- Deviation 3, real-record bodies fetched over the unauthenticated public API: reads only, no contract effect. The seat's to accept.
- `open_questions`: empty. The dev's noted-not-filed item (new refusals of clean text, by design) is answered in ④: the two disclosed forms stand as nits; one undisclosed form is S2.
- The claim's premise correction (the reader lives in `check-half-states.mjs`, not in the two files the card names) is right at this head.
- The body's self-test counts and its 48 gate commands are the dev's local runs; the CI job that runs the tooling self-tests concluded success on this head. Not re-run.

### ④ Design judgment

N1/N2 against the brief: the new rule does refuse a realistic closed finding whose title fits on one line and is followed by an ordinary explanation, on the same line or the next, when the line carries the grade word. That is what the brief teaches and no more: `BRIEF_GRADE_LINES` at this head still says the delta record names what it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`, and that form carries no grade word, so the reader never opens on it and its body is free (pinned by the control cell `- **S1: closed.** Every knock names a key.`). `--template` says nothing on closing and so does not disagree. The guard's unattributable refusal still cites the grade-carrying closed form, which remains valid when the finding ends on its line. All the measured delta records close by id alone. Sound.

N4: `Verdict: FAIL closed`, a `FAIL closed` cell and a heading tail opening with it still read as the verdict word (the bare word is excused only before `-closed`); the idiom forms and a bare caps FAILED line read clean. As pinned.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix) — the arrow spelling still clears on the template's own key.** The reader's loop is `if (explicit) verdicts.push(…); else if (… KEYED …)`. A line `**VERDICT: PASS → FAIL**` (the ASCII arrow likewise) matches `CONTRACT_REVIEW_VERDICT_EXPLICIT`, which stops at the first word, so it counts as one PASS line and the keyed reader, the only one that knows the arrow, never sees it. The record then reads one PASS, no FAIL spelling, and `recordPassVerdict` clears it. The card's N3 names this spelling; the fix and its pin cover it only for a key that is NOT the caps template key (`Verdict:`), which is the less likely place for a seat to write it, since the template line is the one being amended. Same at base, so no regression, but the body calls the spelling closed and its "still outside the reader" list omits it; it is the open direction of the gate. Cure in one place: read an explicit PASS line through the keyed reader as well (it matches this line as written), and pin the caps form.
- **S2 (should-fix) — two stacked grade-key lines no longer read clean.** `contractReviewFindingContinues` ends a finding at a blank line, a block start or a line led by a finding ID; a next line that is itself a grade-led line with no id is treated as a body. So a count block of the two grade keys each valued `none`, on consecutive plain lines, now reads the first as OPEN and the record refuses; at base both cleared, and that key form was taken in as clean by record 6892305129. The docblock says the finding ends at "a new finding", which the code honours only for id-led ones. No measured record stacks them (none uses the key form at all), so this is the weaker of the two; it is a refusal of clean text the body does not disclose, cured by also ending the finding when the next line matches `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED`, with one control cell.
- N1 (nit) — what N1 of the card still leaves, same as base: a body after a blank line inside the same list item, and a next line led by an id with no grade word (`S1 stays open …`) both leave the title closed. The second is the by-id residual already accepted in record 6891926185.
- N2 (nit) — spellings still outside the new table and arrow readers: an arrow inside a cell beside a verdict cell; a table whose header names two verdict columns (only the first is read, so prior-and-current columns miss the second); a cell index shifted by an escaped pipe; the key and word joined by an unspaced hyphen. Each exotic.
- N3 (nit) — two narrowings past the card's list: the idiom lookahead `[ \t-]+closed` also excuses a value followed by a spaced hyphen and then `closed`, and the value `FAILED closed`; the heading mask also drops a late caps `FAILED closed`. Mirroring the idiom regex's own separator would close the first.
- N4 (nit) — new refusals of clean text beyond the two the body discloses: a lower-case `fail-open` or `fails` in a heading tail; a body row whose verdict-column cell opens with the word in a table that tabulates what a reader returned; any later arrow on a keyed line; a struck first word before PASS on a keyed line (the tilde joined the mark class). All toward closed, a repost cures them. The guard's open-finding refusal does not name the remedy (close by id alone, or a blank line); that text is outside the diff, a follow-up.

Did the change break anything else: no. The taught open shapes still read open, the denial forms are untouched, the r3 and round-1 FAIL forms all still match the widened regexes, and the twelve N3 pins, six N4 pins and five N4 controls read as the rows expect when traced by hand.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 each earn a delta review of their fix; both move the head. The four nits can ride the same commit or a follow-up card.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e9e1797782d7887aec9b02229b5222bb16f278c6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (ungoverned; `reviewFace` returns no `hits`) + scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs, scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs (judged as the contract files, per the brief)

DELTA review from `22861e63ff08f3e8cec2a387bff0be185848439e` (record 6898558527) to this head, PR #34054, card #33770. Read: the range between the two heads (one commit of the PR's own, `af85cdbe`, +16 -5 in `check-half-states.mjs` only, and a merge of main `529ed7d9`), the net diff against main (2 files, +102 -25), the PR body at this head, and the check-runs. The merge resolved nothing by hand: both files are byte-identical between `af85cdbe` and this head, the merged main range touches neither, and the diff from `529ed7d9` to this head is those two files alone. `record-recognisers.mjs` moved through main only. Everything below was traced by reading; nothing was run.

Below, the two upper grade words are left unspelled except in the closing denial, so that this record reads as it means under the reader it reviews.

Check-runs on the head, snapshot 2026-11-15T18:05Z: 54 runs; 31 success, 22 skipped, 0 failed, 1 STILL RUNNING: `Live half-state sweep`. Concluded success include `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `Check PR Size`, both PR-body guards and the four type-check families.

### ① Derived judgments

- The explicit-line change moves toward refusal only: an explicit PASS line gains one extra read by `CONTRACT_REVIEW_FAIL_KEYED`; the word pushed to `verdicts` is unchanged, an explicit line of the other word is untouched, and nothing is removed from any reader. Right.
- `opensFinding` moves toward clean, by exactly one class: a next line that `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED` reads as a finding lead now ends the finding above it. That line is then read as a finding of its own in the same loop, so it clears only if it is itself closed or none; a wrapped title or a take-back that opens with the grade word still refuses, on its own line. No open direction gained. `CONTRACT_REVIEW_GRADE_NAMED` has no `g` flag, so `test` keeps no position.
- `CONTRACT_REVIEW_FAIL_WORD` moves toward refusal: as a value only the hyphenated idiom and the one-space plural form are excused; the past form followed by a space or a spaced hyphen and `closed` reads as the verdict word again, as at base.
- One reader still, no new export; the guard file is unchanged in the delta.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `skip-changeset` label present, `Clause-②: no`, `scripts/pm/**` only, nothing published.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No new deviation and no open question in the delta. The three deviations of round 1 stand as answered in record 6898558527.
- The body's counts (5287 / 535 / 399) and its three new ablations are the dev's local runs; the CI job that runs the tooling self-tests concluded success on this head. Not re-run. The body explains the lower third count by main's own change to that file, which agrees with the merge range read here.

### ④ Design judgment

Prior findings, by id:

- **S1: closed.** Traced on the caps template key: `**VERDICT: PASS → FAIL**` matches the explicit reader (one PASS) and then the keyed reader (the lead takes the bold marks, the key is read in any case, the colon, the arrow group, the word), so the line is also a FAIL spelling and `recordPassVerdict` refuses it as self-contradicting. Same with the ASCII arrow, the double arrow, no emphasis, and the arrow followed by the word in bold. Inside a quote the explicit reader still matches and the keyed lead takes the quote mark, so it reads the same way (pinned). Inside a list item, or under a heading mark, the line was never an explicit line; it goes through the keyed reader on the other branch and reads as a FAIL spelling with no verdict line, refused twice over. The plain template line gains no spelling: with no arrow and no struck word after the colon the keyed reader needs its word directly there and finds PASS. A FAIL word that is struck after the PASS value stays clean, which is its meaning. Pinned by one row of six cells, with the dev's ablation named in the body.
- **S2: closed.** The two grade keys each valued none, stacked on plain lines, now clear both lines as at base; so do a bulleted first line over a plain second, and a closed finding over a none-valued key (pinned). The control holds: body text under the first key keeps it open, since the next line is neither a block start nor a finding lead. The quoted branch calls the same predicate. The docblock's "a new finding" is now true of the code.
- N3 of record 6898558527: taken. The value lookahead no longer takes a spaced hyphen or the past form; three pins and two controls, read by hand against the new alternation, give the row's `1,1,1,0,0`.
- N4 of that record: the arrow-on-a-keyed-line and struck-word refusals, the heading-tail `fail-open` case and the still-excused one-space plural value are now in the body's Acceptance notes. Disclosed, stands as accepted.
- N1 and N2 of that record are unchanged and stand as nits for a follow-up.

The four real records of round 1, traced again on this head: 6897840089, 6897742597 and 6892689104 clear; 6898215827 refuses, as at base and at the prior head, for its count line alone. Each carries one plain template verdict line with nothing after the word, no keyed line valued with the past form, and no grade-led line with a state, so none of the three changes reaches them.

New at this head, nits only:

- N5 (nit) — the docblock of `contractReviewRecordReading` still says the past-form idiom with a space is excused "anywhere"; as a key's or cell's value it now reads as the verdict word (the comment on the constant is right, the heading mask still excuses it). Toward refusal; a word in the docblock.
- N6 (nit) — a bulleted grade key valued none with a second grade key indented under it still reads the first as open: the deeper-indent test runs before the new predicate. Toward closed, and nobody indents a sibling key.

Did the delta break anything else: no. Every round-1 pin row is unchanged in the delta and its cells read the same through the changed alternation (the N4 cells use the hyphenated and one-space plural forms, both still excused; the control cells use the bare word before a space, still read).

No must-fix, no should-fix. Two new nits; nits alone end the round.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8nyzh6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
